string.name: check_db_help
string.value:
Checks the integrity of the local card collection and repairs abnormal data.

Issues that may be fixed:
• Invalid card properties or cards missing a note
• Wrong field count, missing or duplicate templates
• Missing decks, invalid review log properties
• Invalid UTF-8 characters, future timestamps
• Corrupt collection file (restore from backup)

When to use:
• You suspect abnormal card data (e.g. cards disappeared, review logs messed up)
• After a sync conflict or a forced app shutdown
• Step 4 of Anki's official troubleshooting flow (Tools → Check Database)

Note: The check rebuilds and optimizes the database; it normally does not lose data. If it reports the collection is corrupt, please restore from an automatic backup.

string.name: deck_learn_steps_help
string.value:
The delays a new card must pass while “learning”. Separate numbers with spaces; the default unit is minutes, and 30s (seconds), 2h (hours), 2d (days) also work.
Again returns to the first step, Good advances to the next, and passing all steps graduates the card into the review queue.

string.name: deck_relearn_steps_help
string.value:

Example: 10 means — a lapsed review card reappears once after 10 minutes and a correct answer returns it to the review queue; empty means it skips the relearning queue and its interval is adjusted directly.

string.name: deck_newPerDay_help
string.value:
The maximum number of new cards introduced each day. If you study fewer than the limit or miss a day, it does not accumulate — the next day starts again at the original limit.
Official advice: new cards sharply increase your near-term review load, so keep this at least 10x smaller than the daily review limit. Official rule of thumb — consistently learning 20 new cards a day stabilizes your daily reviews at about 200.
Example: set to 20 and you learn at most 20 new cards today; the rest roll over to tomorrow.
Note: the review limit also caps new cards — with a review limit of 200 and 190 reviews already waiting, at most 10 new cards appear today; once the review quota is exhausted, new cards stop appearing by default (enable “New cards ignore review limit” in advanced settings to change this).

string.name: deck_reviewsPerDay_help
string.value:
The maximum number of due review cards shown each day; once reached, no more reviews appear even if more are waiting. Interday learning cards count toward this limit before review cards.
Example: set to 200 and even if 300 cards are due, only 200 are shown today; the rest roll over to tomorrow.
This limit also constrains new cards: once the review quota is exhausted, new cards stop appearing by default.
Official tip: the limit is great for smoothing occasional due-date spikes (e.g. returning after a week off); when cards are hidden by the limit, the congratulations screen suggests raising it if you have time.

string.name: deck_learnSteps_help
string.value:
The delays a new card must pass while “learning”. Separate numbers with spaces; the default unit is minutes, and 30s (seconds), 2h (hours), 2d (days) also work.
Again returns to the first step, Good advances to the next, and passing all steps graduates the card into the review queue; Hard follows three official rules: on the first step it shows the average of the first two steps (e.g. 1 10 → 6m); with only one step it shows 1.5x that step (at most 1 day longer); on any later step it repeats the current step.
Example: 1 10 means — a wrong answer repeats after 1 minute, a correct answer repeats after 10 minutes, and another correct answer graduates the card; it then reappears across days per the graduating interval.

string.name: deck_relearnSteps_help
string.value:
The delays a review card must pass again after you press Again and forget it. Same rules as learning steps; may be left empty.
Example: 10 means — a lapsed review card reappears once after 10 minutes and a correct answer returns it to the review queue.
When empty: lapsed cards skip relearning and return to the review queue directly with a new interval (1 day by default).

string.name: deck_newPerDayMinimum_help
string.value: A reserved field marked “currently unused” in the official Anki protocol. Setting it has no effect on scheduling today; it is shown only for compatibility with older deck presets. No need to change it.

string.name: deck_graduatingIntervalGood_help
string.value:
How many days to wait after a new card passes its final learning step with Good before it appears as a review card.
Example: 1 means it graduates today and first appears as a review tomorrow; 3 means it appears 3 days later.
This is a legacy SM-2 option; with FSRS enabled it no longer applies (FSRS computes the first review timing itself).

string.name: deck_graduatingIntervalEasy_help
string.value:
Pressing Easy while learning graduates the card immediately and sets this as its first review interval (days), regardless of remaining learning steps.
Example: 4 means pressing Easy skips the remaining steps and the card reappears as a review in 4 days.
Official validation: the easy interval should be at least as long as the good graduating interval, typically a few days longer. No effect with FSRS enabled.

string.name: deck_newCardInsertOrder_help
string.value:
Controls the initial position (due number) new cards get; lower numbers are learned first. Existing new cards are repositioned when you change this.
“Due order”: first added, first learned. “Random”: new cards get random positions.
Official advice: with the v3 scheduler, keep “Due order” and control draw order via “New card gather order” instead.

string.name: deck_newCardGatherPriority_help
deck_newCardSortOrder_help
deck_newMix_help
string.value:
When new cards appear relative to reviews: mixed with reviews / after reviews / before reviews.
Example: “After reviews” clears today's due reviews before any new cards; “Before reviews” teaches new cards first.

string.name: deck_interdayLearningMix_help
string.value:
Where (re)learning cards that cross days (delay ≥1 day, not yet graduated) appear relative to reviews. Note: interday learning cards are always gathered before reviews and count toward the review limit; this only controls display order.
Official view: learning cards are usually harder than reviews — some prefer them last (finish the easy ones first), others first (more time for cards about to be forgotten).
Example: with “After reviews”, today's due reviews appear first and yesterday's leftover learning cards come last.

string.name: deck_minimumLapseInterval_help
string.value:
The minimum days to wait before a forgotten review card (Again) is shown again after it finishes relearning (or skips it); default is 1 day.
Official validation: this should be at least as long as the final relearning step, otherwise the card would come due before relearning finishes.
Example: 1 means a forgotten card reappears tomorrow at the earliest; 3 means at least 3 days pass, keeping a hard card from repeating too soon.

string.name: deck_leechThreshold_help
string.value:
After a review card is answered Again this many times in total, it is marked as a leech.
Example: 8 means the card becomes a leech on its 8th lapse.
Leeches consume a lot of time. Official advice: rewrite the card, delete it, or devise a mnemonic for it.

string.name: deck_leechAction_help
string.value:
What happens when the leech threshold is reached:
· Tag only: adds a leech tag to the note and shows a notice; the card keeps appearing;
· Suspend card: also hides the card until you manually unsuspend it.
Example: to handle leeches in batches, choose “Tag only”, then find them later in Browse with tag:leech and rewrite them.

string.name: deck_reviewOrder_help
string.value:
The order due review cards are shown. Default is “Due date” — cards waiting longest appear first, clearing the oldest backlog first.
Common choices: Due date (oldest dues first), Interval ascending (short intervals first for quick easy wins), Retrievability descending (most forgettable first), Relative overdueness (most overdue by ratio first), Deck then due date (clear deck by deck).
Example: with a backlog of 500, the default “Due date” shows cards due two weeks ago before cards due yesterday.

string.name: deck_buryNew_help
string.value:
When on: other “new” cards from the same note (e.g. reverse cards, adjacent clozes) won't appear today and roll over to tomorrow.
Example: a note generates both “Front→Back” and “Back→Front” new cards; after you learn the front one today, the back one arrives tomorrow.

string.name: deck_buryReviews_help
string.value:
When on: other “review” cards from the same note won't appear today and roll over to tomorrow.
Example: with two review cards from one note, only one appears today, so neither answer spoils the other.

string.name: deck_buryInterdayLearning_help
string.value:
When on: other interday learning cards (interval >1 day) from the same note won't appear today and roll over to tomorrow.
Background: gathering order is intraday learning → interday learning → reviews → new cards, and a later type cannot bury an earlier type.
Example: with only “Bury new siblings” on, if a note's review card is learned first, its new sibling won't appear today; but learning the new card first does not bury the review sibling.

string.name: deck_disableAutoplay_help
string.value:
When on, card audio no longer plays automatically; tap the play button manually.
Example: enable it in libraries or at night so flipping a card never makes sudden noise.

string.name: deck_skipQuestionWhenReplayingAnswer_help
string.value:
When replaying answer audio, the question part of the audio is skipped.
Example: a card has “question recording + answer recording”; replaying the answer plays only the answer part.

string.name: deck_waitForAudio_help
string.value:
When on, automatic advance (auto show answer / auto continue) waits until audio finishes playing.
Example: combine with “Seconds before showing answer” on listening cards so the card flips only after the recording ends.

string.name: deck_capAnswerTimeToSecs_help
string.value:
The cap (seconds) applied when recording how long an answer took; longer times are recorded as the cap.
Example: the default 60 means a card pondered for 3 minutes is recorded as 60 seconds, keeping study statistics sane when you step away mid-card.

string.name: deck_showTimer_help
string.value:
Shows the time spent on the current card on the study page.
Example: enable it to pace yourself, e.g. answering within 15 seconds per card.

string.name: deck_stopTimerOnAnswer_help
string.value: Freeze the on-screen timer when the answer is shown. Study statistics still include time until you grade the answer.

string.name: deck_secondsToShowQuestion_help
string.value: Wait this many seconds before the question action; 0 disables it. Start or pause Auto advance from More on the study screen.

string.name: deck_secondsToShowAnswer_help
string.value: Wait this many seconds before the answer action; 0 disables it. Start or pause Auto advance from More on the study screen.

string.name: deck_questionAction_help
string.value: When the question countdown ends, show the answer or a reminder. A reminder does not flip the card.

string.name: deck_answerAction_help
string.value: When the answer countdown ends, bury the card, grade it Again/Good/Hard, or show a reminder. Requires Auto advance to be started.

string.name: deck_desiredRetention_help
string.value:
FSRS schedules reviews against this target: a card appears when its predicted recall probability drops to this value.
Example: 0.9 aims for a 90% chance you still remember when the card comes due. Higher (e.g. 0.95) → more frequent reviews and larger daily load; lower (e.g. 0.85) → fewer reviews but more forgetting. Officially recommended range is 0.8–0.97; 0.9 is a common balance.

string.name: deck_fsrsParams4_help
string.value:
The weight list of the legacy FSRS v4, separated by spaces. Kept only for compatibility with historical data; current scheduling uses v6, so you normally don't need to fill this in.
Example: decks imported from an old Anki version may carry v4 parameters; to get valid parameters, use FSRS optimization to compute them automatically.

string.name: deck_easyDaysPercentages_help
string.value:
FSRS workload weights for the 7 days of the week (0–1, separated by spaces, Monday through Sunday). Days with lower weights get reduced review load, redistributed to other days.
Example: 1 1 1 1 1 0.4 0.4 means normal load on weekdays and only ~40% on Saturday and Sunday — a lighter weekend.

string.name: deck_fsrsParams5_help
string.value:
The 19 weights of the legacy FSRS v5, separated by spaces. Kept only for compatibility with historical data; current scheduling uses v6, so you normally don't need to fill this in.
Example: if parameters are missing or broken, leave this empty to fall back to defaults, or rerun optimization to refit them.

string.name: deck_fsrsParams6_help
string.value:
The 21 weights of the current FSRS v6, separated by spaces. They are fitted automatically from your review history by “Optimize”; avoid editing them by hand.
Example: a bad manual edit can derail scheduling — clear the field to restore defaults, or rerun optimization to let the system compute them.

string.name: deck_historicalRetention_help
string.value:
Your actual retention estimated from past reviews, for comparison with “Desired retention”.
Example: a target of 0.9 with a historical 0.83 means cards are too hard or parameters need optimizing; close values mean scheduling matches expectations.

string.name: deck_paramSearch_help
string.value:
Internal search configuration used by FSRS parameter optimization (compatibility/experimental field). No need to fill it in for daily use.
Example: regular users can leave it empty and use the default optimization flow.

string.name: deck_initialEase_help
string.value:
In the legacy (SM-2) algorithm, the initial ease factor for newly graduated cards (2.5 = 250%).
Example: 2.5 means the post-graduation interval starts at “graduating interval × 2.5”.
Only applies when FSRS is disabled.

string.name: deck_easyMultiplier_help
string.value:
In the legacy algorithm, the extra interval multiplier applied when answering Easy (default 1.3).
Example: with a 10-day interval and ease 2.5, Easy gives ≈ 10 × 2.5 × 1.3 = 32.5 days. Only applies when FSRS is disabled.

string.name: deck_hardMultiplier_help
string.value:
In the legacy algorithm, the interval multiplier applied when answering Hard (default 1.2).
Example: with a 10-day interval, Hard gives ≈ 10 × 1.2 = 12 days. Only applies when FSRS is disabled.

string.name: deck_lapseMultiplier_help
string.value:
In the legacy algorithm, after forgetting a review card, new interval = old interval × this multiplier (default 0, i.e. reset and start over).
Example: 0.5 means the interval is halved instead of reset. Only applies when FSRS is disabled.

string.name: deck_intervalMultiplier_help
string.value:
In the legacy algorithm, a global multiplier applied to all review intervals (default 1).
Example: if reviews feel too dense, use 1.1 to stretch every interval by 10%; too loose, use 0.9 to tighten. Only applies when FSRS is disabled.

string.name: deck_maximumReviewInterval_help
string.value:
The upper bound (days) of review intervals; anything longer is capped (default 36500 days = 100 years).
Example: 365 means no matter how long the algorithm's interval is, you'll see the card again within a year, preventing cards from “graduating forever”.

string.name: deck_ignoreRevlogsBeforeDate_help
string.value:
FSRS optimization/evaluation ignores review logs before this date (YYYY-MM-DD); leave empty to use everything.
Example: if your early reviews used messy options, enter 2026-01-01 to fit parameters using only this year's clean data.

string.name: add_note_deck_help
string.value:
Which deck this card is saved into. The deck you were viewing before opening this page is selected by default.
Example: to put a vocabulary card into the “English::CET-4” subdeck, open the dropdown and pick that deck; deck hierarchy is shown with “::”.
Changing the deck only affects where this card is saved, not its content.

string.name: add_note_notetype_help
string.value:
The note type decides which fields this note has and which card templates are generated; the field list below updates when you change it.
Example: “Basic” has just Front/Back fields and makes 1 card; “Basic (and reversed card)” also makes a reverse card; “Cloze” hides text marked {{c1::...}}.
Tip: after switching types, fill fields per their names; saving fails if a required field is empty.

string.name: add_note_notetype_basic_help
string.value:
Purpose: the most basic Q&A note type — one question, one answer. Good for simple memorization like vocabulary, concepts, definitions.
Difference from type-in-the-answer: Basic review is mental recall only; you do not type the answer.
Generates 1 card (Front → Back). During review you see Front, recall Back mentally, then flip to verify.
Field effects: Front holds the question (e.g. “apple”); Back holds the answer (e.g. “apple’s translation”).

string.name: add_note_notetype_basic_reversed_help
string.value:
Purpose: bidirectional Q&A note type. Good for content that must be drilled both ways, e.g. bilingual word pairs.
Difference from plain Basic: an extra reverse card is generated so both directions are tested.
Generates 2 cards (Front → Back + Back → Front). One card asks Front and answers Back; the other is reversed.
Field effects: Front holds the question (e.g. “apple”); Back holds the answer (e.g. “apple’s translation”). Both fields are shared by the two cards.

string.name: add_note_notetype_basic_optional_reversed_help
string.value:
Purpose: optional bidirectional Q&A — decide per note whether to generate the reverse card. Good for mixed decks where only some items need both directions.
Difference from Basic (and reversed card): the reverse card is not always on; the third field Add Reverse controls whether a reverse card is generated.
By default generates 1 forward card (Front → Back); when Add Reverse = “1” or “y”, an extra reverse card (Back → Front) is generated, 2 cards in total.
Field effects: Front holds the question (e.g. “apple”); Back holds the answer (e.g. “apple’s translation”); Add Reverse = “1” or “y” to generate the reverse card, leave empty for forward only.

string.name: add_note_notetype_cloze_help
string.value:
[Purpose] Fill-in-the-blank note type. Delete text in place to test recall. Good for memorizing source text, definitions, example sentences.

[c1–c5 button usage]
① Type the source text in the Text field;
② Select the part to delete;
③ Tap c1/c2/c3/c4/c5 — it wraps the selection as {{cN::selected text}}.
With no selection, tapping inserts an empty marker {{cN::}} and places the cursor right after the colon for typing.

[c index semantics]
· All markers sharing the same c index → deleted together on the same card;
· Different c indices → different cards (c1 is card 1, c2 is card 2, ...).
Example: The {{c1::capital}} of {{c1::France}} is {{c2::Paris}}
  · Card 1 (c1): The [...] of [...] is Paris
  · Card 2 (c2): The capital of France is [...]
This design supports progressive learning — c1 deletes big chunks (learn the whole first), c2/c3 delete details (drill finer points later).

[Difference from Q&A] No separate question is needed; deletions are the questions. One note generates as many cards as distinct c indices.

[Field effects]
· Text: source text with {{c1::answer}} marks, e.g. “The capital of France is {{c1::Paris}}”. During review c1 shows as [...]; recall Paris then flip to reveal.
· Extra: notes or examples, usually left empty.

string.name: add_note_notetype_basic_type_answer_help
string.value:
Purpose: type-in-the-answer Q&A — a variant of Q&A where the back shows an input box; after you submit, the system compares with the correct answer and marks each character red/green.
Difference from regular Q&A: review requires active typing instead of mental recall, better suited for spelling and dictation.
Generates 1 card (Front side, Back side + input box check).
Field effects: Front holds the question (e.g. “apple”); Back holds the answer (e.g. “apple”). During review the input box accepts your typing, then is compared against this field.

string.name: add_note_notetype_image_occlusion_help
string.value: Purpose: used to memorize by drawing masks on an image (e.g. anatomy labels, map place names). Suited for image-based memory. Difference from regular Q&A: image + masks replace text Q&A — instead of deleting text, you draw rectangles on the image to cover the regions to be tested. Each mask index generates one card. During review the mask covers the region; flip to reveal the underlying image. Field effects: pick an image, draw rectangular masks, optionally fill in header and extra. Image: after picking, the system writes it and fills for you, no manual entry. Occlusions: open the mask editor and draw one or more rectangles, each tied to a c index; the system auto-generates the {{c1::image-occlusion:rect:...}} string, no manual entry. Header: optional, a title shown at the top of the card (e.g. “Upper limb muscles”). Back Extra: optional, extra text shown after flipping.

string.name: add_note_tags_help
string.value:
Tags for this note; separate multiple tags with spaces. Tags are independent of decks and are used for cross-deck search and filtering; “::” creates hierarchy.
Example: entering “english cet4::listening” adds both the “english” and “cet4::listening” tags, later searchable via tag:english or tag:cet4::listening.
Leave empty for no tags.

string.name: deck_reviewLimit_help
string.value:
A daily review limit that applies only to this deck, overriding the preset; leave blank to follow the preset.
Example: with a preset of 200 reviews/day, entering 50 for the “Medicine” deck caps Medicine at 50 reviews a day, while decks using the preset are unaffected.

string.name: deck_newLimit_help
string.value:
A daily new-card limit that applies only to this deck, overriding the preset; leave blank to follow the preset.
Example: with a preset of 20 new cards/day, entering 5 for the “Speaking” deck introduces at most 5 new cards there each day.

string.name: deck_reviewToday_help
string.value:
A temporary review limit for today only; it expires tomorrow. Leave blank to clear the temporary value.
Example: short on time today, set the limit to 50; tomorrow it automatically reverts to the preset.

string.name: deck_newToday_help
string.value:
A temporary new-card limit for today only; it expires tomorrow. Leave blank to clear the temporary value.
Example: to push harder today, raise the new-card limit to 40; it automatically reverts tomorrow.

string.name: deck_reviewTodayActive_help
string.value:
Whether “Today's review limit” is currently in effect: the temporary value above applies only while this is on; when off, the value is kept but not applied today.
Example: 50 is entered but the switch is off, so today still follows the preset limit.

string.name: deck_newTodayActive_help
string.value:
Whether “Today's new-card limit” is currently in effect: the temporary value applies only while this is on; when off, the value is kept but not applied today.
Example: 40 is entered but the switch is off, so today still follows the preset new-card limit.

string.name: deck_desiredRetentionOverride_help
string.value:
An FSRS desired retention that applies only to this deck, overriding the preset; leave blank to follow the preset.
Example: with a preset of 0.9, entering 0.95 for the “High-frequency exam points” deck schedules it more densely while other decks stay at 0.9.

string.name: deck_newCardsIgnoreReviewLimit_help
string.value:
By default, new cards stop appearing once the review limit is exhausted; when on, new cards appear regardless of the review limit.
Example: the 200-card review limit is fully consumed by reviews — with this on, new cards still appear today (making the day's total load heavier). This is a collection-wide setting affecting all decks.

string.name: deck_fsrsEnabled_help
string.value:
Enables the FSRS scheduling algorithm for the whole collection (replacing the legacy SM-2). FSRS fits a memory model from your review history and typically reduces review load at the same retention.
Note: this is a collection-wide switch affecting all decks; after enabling, run parameter optimization once.

string.name: deck_applyAllParentLimits_help
string.value:
By default, studying from a child deck ignores the daily limits of decks above it; when on, limits apply level by level starting from the topmost deck.
Example: “Languages” (limit 50) contains “English” (limit 30); with this on, studying from English is also bounded by Languages' 50 — both levels constrain at once. Useful for capping an entire deck tree. This is a collection-wide setting.

string.name: deck_fsrsReschedule_help
string.value:
On save, also recalculate due dates for cards that need updating because of changes to parameters, desired retention, or related options. Leave off to avoid immediate rescheduling.
Changes apply only to this deck by default. Enabling shared changes also affects the related decks. Toggling the global FSRS switch affects all decks.
Large collections may take longer. Wait for saving to finish.

string.name: deck_fsrsHealthCheck_help
string.value:
Runs a health check on FSRS scheduling data when saving and repairs abnormal states.
Example: if you suspect corrupted scheduling data, save once with this on to let the system self-check and repair; keep it off otherwise.

string.name: glossary_bury_help
string.value:
Skip this card for today. It becomes available again on the next study day.

Skip today is Anki's Bury action. It removes the card from today's study queue without deleting it. The study day follows the app's daily rollover time, which may differ from midnight.

Use it when you want to skip a card today. If you forgot the answer, choose Again so scheduling reflects your recall.

Unlike Suspend card, Skip today restores availability automatically.

To restore it sooner, choose Restore skipped cards on the study completion screen, or select it in Browse and use Restore Cards. The deck options for burying siblings apply the same action automatically to avoid related cards revealing each other's answers.

string.name: glossary_suspend_help
string.value:
Stop reviewing this card until you manually restore it.

This is Anki's Suspend action. It affects the current card, without pausing the whole study session or deleting the card.

Use it for cards you do not need to study for a while. To skip only today, use Skip today. If you forgot the answer, choose Again.

To restore the card, select it in Browse and use Restore Cards.

A card cannot be both buried and suspended. Suspending a skipped card prevents its automatic restoration.

string.name: glossary_delete_help
string.value:
Deletes only the current card; other cards of the same note (e.g. reverse cards) are not affected. If this is the only card of its note, the note will also be removed.

Differs from Anki desktop's More > Delete Note: Anki desktop deletes the entire note and all its cards; jidecards uses the backend RemoveCards path, which removes only the specified card (consistent with AnkiDroid's Delete Card).

You can recover via the "Undo" button at the top of the study screen (the undo stack records the deletion).

Note: deletion is a destructive action; tapping it shows a confirmation dialog.

string.name: glossary_undo_help
string.value:
Undo the previous action, such as a rating, Skip today, Suspend card, or deletion. This corresponds to Anki's Undo.

On the study screen, open More > Undo. It is available when there is an action to undo.

Undo history does not persist across app sessions.

string.name: glossary_ratings_help
string.value:
Recall the answer, tap Show Answer, then rate your recall.

Again: You forgot or answered incorrectly.
Hard: You answered correctly with difficulty.
Good: You recalled the answer normally.
Easy: You answered correctly without effort.

The time below each button estimates when this card will be reviewed again if you choose that rating. Rate your recall, rather than the delay you prefer.

Hard still means your answer was correct. Choose Again if you forgot or answered incorrectly. The scheduler calculates intervals from your progress and deck options. Actual timing may vary slightly; you do not need to wait on the card.

string.name: glossary_leech_help
string.value:
A review card is marked as a leech after it has been rated "Again" a certain number of times (default 8, configurable via "Leech Threshold").

Action options: Tag Only (adds a "leech" tag to the note, card still appears) / Suspend Card (hides the card until manually unsuspended).

Leeches consume a lot of time. Anki official advice: rewrite the card, delete it, or think of a mnemonic — don't just keep lapsing on it.

Configurable via deck options "Leech Threshold" and "Leech Action".

string.name: glossary_siblings_help
string.value:
Multiple cards generated from the same note, e.g. a front→back card and a back→front card, or different cloze deletions from the same text.

Sibling problem: seeing multiple cards of the same note in one session may spoil answers (the back of one card is the front of another).

Anki can auto-bury siblings via deck options "Bury siblings" (separate settings for new and review cards), spreading them across different days.

Note: Anki does not bury siblings that are in learning (time-sensitive).

string.name: glossary_graduating_interval_help
string.value:
The first interval applied when a new card finishes its last learning step and becomes a review card.

Graduating on "Good": uses "Graduating Interval (Good)" (default 1 day, i.e. appears tomorrow as a review card)
Graduating on "Easy": skips remaining steps, uses "Graduating Interval (Easy)" (default 4 days)

This is an SM-2 option; with FSRS enabled, the first review timing is computed by FSRS and this option no longer applies.

string.name: glossary_fsrs_retention_help
string.value:
FSRS schedules reviews to bring cards back when the predicted recall probability drops to this value.

Default 0.9 (90%); official recommended range 0.8–0.97.
Higher (e.g. 0.95) → more frequent reviews, larger daily load, better retention; lower (e.g. 0.85) → fewer reviews but more forgetting.

0.9 is the common balance point. Configurable via deck option "Desired Retention".

string.name: glossary_fuzz_help
string.value:
After a review card's next due date is computed from the rating, Anki applies a small random offset so cards introduced at the same time with the same rating don't always fall on the same day and cluster together.

Learning cards also receive up to 5 minutes of extra delay so they don't always appear in the same order (the next-due text on the rating buttons does not reflect this delay).

Official note: this feature cannot be turned off.

string.name: glossary_shortcuts_help
string.value:
The review screen supports external / Bluetooth / 2-in-1 built-in keyboards with keybindings aligned to Anki desktop:

• Space / Enter: in question phase, show answer; in answer phase, rate "Good"
• 1 / 2 / 3 / 4: in answer phase, rate "Again / Hard / Good / Easy"
• * or B: bury current card (auto-recovers tomorrow)
• @ or S: suspend current card (hidden until manually unsuspended)
• Delete: delete current card (with confirmation dialog)
• Ctrl+Z: undo last action
• Esc: go back to previous screen
• R: replay current-side audio (silent no-op if no audio)

The letter keys B / S / R are easy-to-reach alternatives for keyboards without a numpad; they coexist with the symbol keys * @ — either works.

string.name: glossary_lapse_help
string.value:
A lapse occurs when a review card is rated "Again"; the card enters the relearning flow.

Relearning flow: the card reappears according to the "Relearning Steps" (default 10 minutes); after passing, the new interval starts at the "Minimum Lapse Interval" (default 1 day).

Each lapse increments the card's lapse count; reaching the "Leech Threshold" marks it as a leech.

With FSRS enabled, the post-lapse interval is recomputed by FSRS based on memory_state, no longer using the legacy "Lapse Multiplier".

string.name: glossary_browser_info_help
string.value:
In the browser, tap the ⓘ icon on the right of a card row to view that card's details:

· Card state: New / Learning / Review / Suspended / Buried
· Scheduling: due date, interval, ease, review count, lapse count
· Review history: dates and ratings of recent reviews

Card info is a read-only view. To edit content, tap the card row to enter the edit area.

string.name: browser_help_sidebar_body
string.value:
Tap "Filter" to open the sidebar for quick filtering by deck, tag, or saved search.

· Tap deck/tag: replaces current search with deck: or tag: filter

· Saved searches: uses search strings saved in Anki desktop
· Sections can be collapsed/expanded, state is saved automatically

string.name: browser_help_find_replace_body
string.value:
Batch find and replace text in card fields, mirroring Anki desktop's Find & Replace.

[Inputs]
· Find: text or regex to search for; empty find does nothing
· Replace with: replacement text; empty means delete matches (clear the found text)
· Field name: empty = search all fields; specify a field name (e.g. Front/Back) to restrict to that field; use Tags to replace tags
· Regex: when checked, Find is treated as a regex; use () capture groups and refer to them as $1, $2 in Replace
· Match case: when checked, matches are case-sensitive (Cat does not match cat)

[Scope]
· Selected notes only: replaces only notes currently selected in multi-select mode (long-press a card to enter multi-select first)
· All notes: replaces all notes returned by the current search (constrained by the search box, e.g. deck:Swahili only replaces notes in that deck)

[Examples]
· Replace color with colour everywhere: Find color, Replace colour, Field empty, Scope All notes
· Strip all whitespace from a field: Find \s+, Replace empty, check Regex
· Replace only a specific field of selected cards: Field Back, Scope Selected notes only

[Notes]
· Replace cannot be undone; confirm the scope before executing
· Tags are space-separated, e.g. important hard

string.name: browser_help_batch_body
string.value:
Long-press a card to enter multi-select mode, then batch-operate on selected cards. The descriptions below mirror the Anki desktop Cards / Notes menus (see official manual browsing.html#menus-and-actions).

[Change Deck]
Move selected cards to another deck. Equivalent to Anki Cards menu > Change Deck. Both new and review cards can be moved; scheduling state is preserved.

[Set Flag]
Assign a color flag (red / orange / green / blue) to selected cards. In Anki, flags only mark cards for attention in the browser and review; they do not affect scheduling. Choose "None" to clear an existing flag.

[Suspend]
Pause scheduling of selected cards; suspended cards will not appear in study. Equivalent to Anki's Suspend. Use "Restore" to unsuspend at any time.

[Restore]
Unsuspend selected cards so they re-enter scheduling. Equivalent to Anki's Unsuspend.

[Delete]
Permanently delete selected cards. If a note has no remaining cards after deletion, the note is also deleted. This cannot be undone — use with care.

[Set Due Date]
Manually set the due date of cards, mirroring Anki Cards menu > Set Due Date.
- New cards are turned into review cards and become due on the specified date
- Range input is supported, e.g. `60-90` means due in 60 to 90 days (randomly distributed across selected cards)
- Review cards keep their interval by default; appending `!` to the range (e.g. `60-90!`) forces rescheduling with a new interval
- Manual scheduling does not record answer time, so review stats are unaffected

[Reposition]
Change the order new cards will appear in the study queue, mirroring Anki Cards menu > Reposition. Only affects new cards; review cards are unaffected.
- Start position: selected cards are assigned numbers starting from this value
- Step: when multiple cards are selected, numbers increment by this step (default 1)
- Random: randomly distribute numbers within each step starting from the start position
- Shift existing: when enabled, inserts new positions between existing cards and pushes higher-positioned cards back (e.g. inserting 3/4/5 between 1 and 2 yields 1/3/4/5/2); when disabled, cards may share a position number with existing cards and the order becomes unpredictable. When enabled, all higher-positioned cards are modified and must be sent on the next sync

[Change Note Type]
Convert selected notes from one type to another, mirroring Anki Notes menu > Change Note Type. For example, changing cards mistakenly created as Basic into Cloze. You must manually map old fields / templates to new ones; unmapped field data will be lost.
- Card scheduling is not affected
- Changing note type requires a one-way sync (the next sync can only push, not pull)

[Notes Mode]
Suspend and Restore Cards work in both Cards and Notes modes. Selecting a note applies the action to every card generated by that note. Other card-only batch actions still require Cards mode.

string.name: browser_find_regex_help
string.value:
When checked, the Find box is treated as a regex pattern. Common syntax:

· Character classes: [a-z], \d, \w, \s, etc.
· Quantifiers: *, +, ?, {n,m}
· Anchors: ^ start of line, $ end of line
· Capture groups: () referenced as $1, $2 in Replace
· Escaping: to match special chars like . * ( ) literally, prefix with \

Examples:
· Match digits: \d+
· Match lines starting with hello: ^hello.*
· Reformat date (\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2}) → $3/$2/$1

string.name: stats_help_today
string.value:
Today
Shows review statistics for today.

· Answered: total times you answered cards today (a card may be answered multiple times)
· Correct: reviews where you didn't press Again
· Learn/Review/Relearn/Early: counts for learning new cards, reviewing due cards, relearning failed cards, and reviewing early
· Mature correct: correct / total for mature cards (interval ≥ 21 days)
· Time: total time spent reviewing today

Today's stats are not a good overall indicator; everyone has good and bad days.

string.name: stats_help_forecast
string.value:
Future Due
Shows an estimated number of reviews that will be due on each future day, assuming you learn no new cards and fail no cards (Anki official Future Due).

· X-axis: future dates, near on the left to far on the right; range switchable between 1 month / 3 months / 1 year / all
· Y-axis (bar height): cards due on that day
· Bar colour: dark → light green marks near → far dates (colour only marks the date; bar height is the due count)
· Total: total cards due within the selected range
· Average: daily average of cards due
· Due tomorrow: cards due tomorrow
· Daily load: estimate based on card intervals (sum of 1/interval; intervals < 1 day count as 1)
· Includes backlog: when the in-chart 'Backlog' checkbox is checked, bars on the negative (left) side show overdue but unreviewed cards

Note: the forecast graph does not count reviews that are currently overdue; check the backlog checkbox to see them.

string.name: stats_help_card_counts
string.value:
Card Counts
Shows the distribution of card states in your deck/collection.

· New: never studied
· Learning: in learning phase
· Relearning: failed and re-entering learning
· Young: graduated, interval < 21 days
· Mature: interval ≥ 21 days
· Suspended: manually paused
· Buried: temporarily hidden until next day

Top stacked horizontal bar: each segment's length is the proportion of that card state, ordered left to right as new, learning, relearning, young, mature (plus suspended and buried when 'Separate suspended/buried cards' is checked). The table below lists exact counts and percentages.

string.name: stats_help_hours
string.value:
Hourly Breakdown
Shows your review volume by hour of day.

· X-axis: 24 hours of the day (0-23)
· Left Y-axis (bar height): number of cards studied at that hour
· Bar colour: the larger the volume, the darker the blue

Helps you find the hours you study most.

string.name: stats_help_ease
string.value:
Card Ease / Card Difficulty
Shows the distribution of card difficulty.

· SM-2: shows ease factor distribution (130%-390%) with average ease
· FSRS: shows difficulty distribution (0%-100%; higher = harder)
· X-axis: difficulty, low on the left to high on the right
· Y-axis (bar height): number of cards in that difficulty range
· Bar colour: green → yellow → red means easier → harder

With SM-2, the lower the ease, the more frequently a card will appear. With FSRS, the higher the difficulty, the slower stability will increase.

string.name: stats_help_interval
string.value:
Intervals
Shows the distribution of current review intervals.

· X-axis: review interval (days), short on the left to long on the right
· Y-axis (bar height): number of cards in that interval range
· Bar colour: light → dark blue marks short → long intervals (colour only marks the interval range; bar height is the card count)

Interval = the delay between two reviews. Independent of FSRS: this graph always shows actual card intervals (Anki official Review Intervals).

The time range setting affects this graph differently: it limits displayed interval range, not which cards are included.

string.name: stats_help_stability
string.value:
Stability
Only shown when FSRS is enabled.

· X-axis: stability (days), low on the left to high on the right
· Y-axis (bar height): number of cards in that stability range
· Bar colour: light → dark blue marks low → high stability (colour only marks the stability range; bar height is the card count)

Stability = the amount of time required for the probability of recall to decrease from 100% to 90%. Higher stability = less likely to be forgotten (Anki official Card Stability). Note: intervals reflect actual scheduling, while stability reflects memory strength.

string.name: stats_help_retention
string.value:
Retention
Pass rate of cards with an interval ≥ 1 day (Anki official True Retention table).

· Young: review cards with interval < 21 days
· Mature: cards with interval ≥ 21 days
· Pass: pressed Hard, Good or Easy (not Again)
· Fail: pressed Again

Only the first review per day counts.

If you are using FSRS, your retention is expected to be close to your desired retention. Please keep in mind that data for a single day is noisy, so it's better to look at monthly data. If the gap is large, consider optimizing your FSRS parameters, using different presets, suspending/reformulating leeches, or checking your button usage.

string.name: stats_help_retrievability
string.value:
Card Retrievability
Only shown when FSRS is enabled.

· Retrievability = the probability of recalling a card today
· Average: mean retrievability across all reviewed cards
· Estimated known: average retrievability × number of cards reviewed at least once
· X-axis: retrievability (%), low on the left to high on the right
· Y-axis (bar height): number of cards in that probability range
· Bar colour: red → yellow → green means low → high retrievability

Retrievability is calculated by FSRS based on card stability and elapsed time. It is the core metric for FSRS scheduling.

string.name: stats_help_calendar
string.value:
Calendar
A yearly heatmap of daily review counts.

· Each cell is one day: columns are weeks, rows are weekdays; darker color = more reviews that day
· Use ◄ ► to browse previous years (back to 2000 with All-time range)
· Tap a weekday label on the left to change the first day of week (Sunday/Monday/Friday/Saturday)

Matches the Anki official Calendar graph.

string.name: stats_help_reviews
string.value:
Reviews
Daily review counts as a stacked bar chart (Anki official Reviews).

· X-axis: dates, oldest on the left to newest on the right
· Y-axis (bar height): review count per day (or time spent answering when 'Time' is checked)
· Each bar is one day (or a few days merged)
· Stack bottom-up: mature (dark green), young (light green), relearn (red), learn (orange), filtered (purple)
· Check 'Time' to switch to the time taken to answer the questions each day
· Bottom stats: days studied, total, average per day, average on studied days; time mode adds average answer time (seconds/card + cards/minute)

Matches the Anki official Reviews graph.

string.name: stats_help_buttons
string.value:
Answer Buttons
How many times you pressed each answer button (Anki official Answer Buttons).

· Three groups: learning, young and mature cards
· Each group's X-axis, left to right: again, hard, good, easy
· Y-axis (bar height): times that button was pressed
· Bar colors: again red, hard yellow, good light green, easy dark green
· Correct rate shown under each group (any button other than Again counts as correct)
· Time range switchable (default 1 year)

Matches the Anki official Answer Buttons graph.

string.name: stats_help_added
string.value:
Added
The number of cards you have added each day (Anki official Added).

· X-axis: dates, oldest on the left to newest on the right
· Y-axis (bar height): cards added that day
· Bars fade from deep blue (recent) to light blue (oldest)
· Bottom stats: total and average cards per day

Matches the Anki official Added graph.
